searches.answer: The sources indicate that cloud computing trends are heavily influenced by Generative AI, with hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud competing on the power and integration of their GenAI platforms. AWS is noted for its Trainium2 instances for AI training, while Azure is enhancing its OpenAI Service with expanded generative AI model support. Quantum computing in the cloud is also emerging, with all three major hyperscalers offering "Quantum-as-a-Service" platforms. The market share analysis shows AWS leading with approximately 31–32% in Q3 2024, followed by Azure with 20–25%, and Google Cloud with 11–13%. The strategic conversation has shifted from the speed of adopting public cloud to determining the optimal placement of workloads, with AWS and Azure making significant moves to interconnect their services.

searches.answer: Kubernetes 1.20 announced the removal of Docker runtime support in future releases, currently planned for version 1.22. The Docker runtime is not compliant with the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) for Kubernetes, and platforms like Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and Red Hat OpenShift have already moved to other container runtimes such as containerd or CRI-O. Docker Desktop release notes indicate updates to Kubernetes, cri-dockerd, CNI plugins, containerd, and runc, with Kubernetes v1.34.3 and Linux kernel v6.12.72 as of 2026-03-02. The Kubernetes blog confirms the deprecation of Docker as a container runtime after v1.20, advising users to switch to compliant runtimes like containerd or CRI-O.

results.title: Container Runtimes | Kubernetes
results.content:
#### Note:

Kubernetes releases before v1.24 included a direct integration with Docker Engine, using a component named dockershim. That special direct integration is no longer part of Kubernetes (this removal was announced as part of the v1.20 release). You can read Check whether Dockershim removal affects you to understand how this removal might affect you. To learn about migrating from using dockershim, see Migrating from dockershim.
